summary: Input queue capacity (max_records, max_pending, max_retained_bytes) now counts only live (received) inputs via incrementally maintained live index and live_bytes; terminal inputs no longer consume capacity but stay in the projection for idempotency, inputs_for_turn, List and projection repair. Replay split into side-effect-free check() + infallible apply(), so persist no longer clones the whole projection per mutation and Applied/steer checks are O(live) instead of O(history log history). recover() uses a bounded process-wide fold cache keyed by (journal path, session id, limits) and only folds events appended since the cached prefix; the cache is used only if the store still holds the identical last event and last queue event at the cached indices, otherwise it falls back to a full replay.

notes: No src/core.rs change. Behavior change: saturation_preserves_previous_queue_and_journal previously asserted lifetime record exhaustion; updated to assert live-only capacity and that terminal IDs stay reserved (duplicate enqueue is idempotent). Terminal inputs are not compacted out of memory because they back duplicate-ID idempotency, inputs_for_turn, List and repair_projections; SessionStore already keeps every event in memory, so memory remains O(history) as before. recover() still clones the cached projection (memory copy, no JSON parse/replay). repair_projections still iterates all applied inputs per boundary (out of scope). pending_received() now yields receipt (sequence) order instead of ID order. Fold cache risk: a journal at the same path replaced with a different prefix but identical last event and last queue event at the same indices would reuse stale state; considered practically unreachable.
